newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up on speculation.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up on speculation.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly up on Tuesday on speculative buying at low levels, traders said.
The most active June 1997 contract ended at an intraday high of 23,600 yuan ($2,845) per tonne, rising 230 yuan. It opened at a low of 23,200.
March was the only losing contract, falling 20 to 23,180.
April rose 50 to 23,350, May 260 to 23,600, July 240 to 23,600, August 160 to 23,480.
Combined volume fell to 36,900 tonnes from 39,210 tonnes.

The contracts opened lower on overnight losses on the London Metal Exchange but speculative buying push them to rise steadily for almost all the session before most of them closed at their intraday highs, traders said.
"Some speculators took advantage of low prices at the opening to build long positions, pushing prices up for almost the whole session," one trader said.

Traders said the day's gains were also due to strong spot copper prices, which have been rising consistently since the lunar new year holiday in early February. Market sentiment was up with the approach of high comsumption season, they said.
"Investors have confidence in near-term trends with the high consumption season drawing near," said a second trader.
"This is why copper futures have been able to stand firm for quite a number of days up to now," he added.
Analysts expected copper to move between 23,200 yuan and 23,800 yuan per tonne in the next few days.
Aluminium ended down across the board. March fell 120 to 15,800, April 70 to 16,180, May 130 to 16,450 and June 200 to 16,700. Combined volume rose to 2,750 tonnes from 610.
